prometheus.label.service_name.answers: the role that emitted a series -- processor/orchestrator/keeper/webapi; ResourceBuilder.AddService(serviceName:) on both the logs and metrics resources. The Prometheus exporter also derives exported_job from it
prometheus.label.service_name.never_for: picking out one replica -- every replica of the same role shares one service_name; use service_instance_id for that

prometheus.label.service_instance_id.answers: the replica identity carried by every Prometheus series -- InstanceId.Resolve(), the same identity that names a replica's liveness key and reply queue
prometheus.label.service_instance_id.never_for: grouping on instance for a per-replica question -- instance is the scrape target address, and every replica behind one scrape config can share it; service_instance_id is the label that is actually unique per replica. This is the one trap that applies to almost every prometheus.pipeline_* surface in this catalog

prometheus.label.processorId.answers: the processor's database identity, present on a processor host's metrics resource only -- ResourceAttribute("ProcessorId", "processorId", identity.Id) passed to AddBaseConsoleObservability. The metric-side key is the camelCase processorId (MetricKey); the differently-cased ProcessorId is only the log-side key (LogKey), used on log records instead
prometheus.label.processorId.never_for: expecting this label on an orchestrator, keeper, or webapi series -- it is stamped only on a processor host's resource, since name and version alone cannot distinguish two builds of the same processor row
